It's hard to justify saying that I enjoyed my time, which I did. There is something lovely about getting the right combos off after grinding and practicing the movement. The huge BUT in the room is the game is not well balanced. 

It can be beaten, and it will feel good to finally reach the end, but there will be a lot of moments where you just have to put up with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. That said, I think it is worth a try if you ever catch the game for 10 bucks. There is a momentum this game captures that I dont get out of risk of rain. That said AGAIN, I do think the devs took a lot of concepts that sounded like meaningful choices to make on paper at face value. Tons of items to the experienced rougelike fan will be objectively always good, while others are deceptively good until you understand what the game is really asking you to do. 

There is enough nuance to get different playstyles, keep the game fresh especially if you get the cloak to more easily get meta progression money. Doing it that way even teaches you how to not rely on the items and thus learn what items are actually good, but the game devs did not build it to be learnt that way. I recommend this game because it hearkens back to a time when game devs were experimenting, trying new things. It isnt breaking new ground, but there is an earnest attempt to give the player something they would want to play themselves. 

And then they learned nothing in the second game. Which makes this series a deeply fascinating literature type thing to look at if that makes sense.

「1-1突破するだけで50回はリトライしたんだけど・・・」
「たった50回で突破できるようになったの！？」
50という数字は適当ですが、とにかくそんな会話が出てきそうな雰囲気のゲームです。
難しいぞぉ・・・！

このゲームの難しさはとにもかくにも、敵の隙がすごく少ない事。
「あからさまな空振り」「大技後の硬直」「態勢を立て直す時間をくれるぼっ立ちやにらみ合い動作」「ガードブレイクしてピヨピヨ」、他のアクションゲームでは当たり前のそういう隙が、このゲームではほとんどありません。あからさまに雑魚でーすというビジュアルの敵でも、こちらを見つけ次第すごいスピードで駆け寄ってきて休む間もなく体当たりしてきます。

いや、ありますよ、隙。
1フレームとか2フレームとか、そういうレベルでね。

ただ、その理不尽な難しさがあってもなお、このゲームは楽しい。

まず。その理不尽な難しさに慣れて、理不尽にノックアウトされてきた敵に対応できるようになった時の達成感がすごい。
慣れれば隙が見えるようになってくる、そういう風にちゃんと作られてるんですね。
見えるようになるまではすげー大変ですが・・・。

次に、魔法が多種多様で、集めるのも楽しいし、それぞれを使いこなしていくのも楽しい。
自分の好きな属性で固めるもよし、見た目や連続HIT数で選んでもいいし。
自分なりに組み上げた魔法デッキで上手くコンボが決められるようになると、これもまた達成感を味わうことができます。

最後に、死にゲーとしてのテンポの良さとルールの単純さですかね。
死んだらポンポンポンとリザルトを出してホームに帰還。
ダンジョンで手に入れたものは通貨以外全部ロスト。
はい、また一からがんばって。
長ったらしい死亡演出とかホームでのイベントとかそういうのはなく、すぐに何度でもリトライできます。待たされるとしたらダンジョン突入時の生成時間ぐらいですかね。
ゲームとしてリズム、テンポがいいです。

おススメですが「クリアできるようにはなっているけどクリアさせるつもりはないゲーム」であることを念頭に置いた上で買ってください。

After a while, the game can feel repetitive, but that's more a genre issue than a flaw of the game itself. I wish the game had a few different soundtracks for each elemental region, though.

Overall, it's a good and enjoyable experience.

This game is fun at first when you are figuring it out, but after that the game has nothing to offer you My main gripe about this game is about the main bosses. They seem to have been designed solely to look cool with no consideration on how it feels to fight them. The battles start with the boss stringing together random attacks, then pausing to let the player hit them. This idea works well in many games, but it is implemented incredibly poorly in Wizard of Legend. This is because some sequences of attacks are straight up impossible to dodge. The game clearly intends the player to be able to dodge every attack. You can dodge each of the attacks if they are on their own,  and there is an achievement to beat a boss hitless. It does not make sense sense to make undodgeable attacks, but the game did so.

The boss that caused me to write this review was Ice Queen Freiya. If you encounter her as the second boss or later, she gains access to a sweeping beam attack that hits everything in front of her. To dodge it, you must move behind her. This attack works well in isolation, but there was obviously no thought put into how to works with the rest of the fight. There are two separate situations in which this attack becomes undodgeable.

1. Freiya is in a corner
Your spells do knockback, so Freiya often gets knocked into a corner. If she does the beam attack while in the corner, then there is no way to get behind her and dodge the attack.
2. You are too far away
Freiya has several attacks that push away the player. She has two separate AOE that will push you towards the edge of the arena, and if she uses the beam attack after those, there is not enough time to get behind her.
The rest of the game seems to be designed to let you dodge everything if you are good enough, so it simply seems like an oversight to make this attack undodgeable.

While I believe that Frost Queen Freiya is the worst boss, the other bosses also have oversights. Flame Empress Zeal has a meteor attack that covers the entire arena. The problem is that the graphics of the meteors obscure your screen, making it extremely difficult to tell where you are, and if a meteor is going to hit you. Earth Lord Atlas and Wind Sovereign Shuu have homing attacks. These attacks take a long time to expire, and I have had them travel completely off the screen and do a 180 to hit me well after the boss was stunned. And all of the bosses have too small of a window of vulnerability. I find that if I hesitate for even a moment when the boss is vulnerable, I will miss the window and deal almost no damage to them. I believe that the player should be rewarded for surviving the boss attacks instead of constantly missing the window.

Overall, the game falls short on the bosses. They should be the main feature of any roguelike, but they are not enjoyable here. The only boss that I had fun fighting was Master Sura. The rest feel bad to fight against. I do not recommend this game with its bosses in their current form. I do not think I would enjoy those bosses unless the attacks are completely redesigned to not allow them to be unavoidable.

The presentation of using combos to get through the dungeon is somewhat misleading, as spamming your abilities works, and combos against bosses in particular usually end up putting you in a bad position more times than not. 

Yes, there's many different relics and combinations of items, but most of the spells presented in the game feel underwhelming and unsatisfying to land simply due to either the lack of impact or lackluster damage they present. The items and curses are either hit or miss, either they buff your run a tad bit, or they nerf badly.

Beating the bosses doesn't feel rewarding either, as the "final bosses" of an area feel like a pushover even at the higher stages of the dungeon. Beating them has no weight because they simply teleport and disappear once you beat them.

Overall, I wouldn't recommend this game, each run played is either a hit or miss, Every combat encounter ends up with you easily clearing the enemies or getting stunlocked until death. But for it's price it's an okay way to pass the time. The game isn't for everyone, it isn't my taste after some reflection, so I'd still recommend trying it if you desire too. It was an okay game, forgettable, but okay for its price.
